extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collected from multiple existing datasets including Fleurs (new recordings from FLoRes sentences), MLS (derived from Librivox audiobooks), VoxPopuli (from European Parliament sessions), CoVoST-2, and Minds-14. Fleurs recordings collected with 1-3 recordings per sentence.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs: FLoRes dev and devtest sentences with new recordings; MLS: Librivox audiobooks; VoxPopuli: European Parliament sessions; CoVoST-2: speech translation corpus; Minds-14: e-banking domain spoken data
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Fleurs: new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets. Minds-14: monolingual datasets merged into a single multilingual dataset with 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 to 3 recordings per sentence for Fleurs
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language, geography (102 languages from different geographical regions and language families)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction. Tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for speech recognition, speech translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval tasks. Designed for few-shot learning and evaluation of multilingual speech representation learning. Training sets range from a few hours to a few hundred hours of labeled data per language.

name.evidence: We introduce XTREME-S, a new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages.

description.evidence: XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval. Covering 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families, XTREME-S aims to simplify multilingual speech representation evaluation, as well as catalyze research in "universal" speech representation leaming.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets, in 102languages. We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2:3on average). The Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset is a large corpus derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli is a multilingual speech dataset for semi-supervised leaming. It contains 400k hours of unannotated speech as well as speech transcriptions and translations.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Fleurs is the speech version of the FLoRes machine translation benchmark. We use 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets. The Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset is a large corpus derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli is a multilingual speech dataset for semi-supervised leaming. MINDS-14 is an intent classification task from spoken data. It covers 14 intents extracted from the e-banking domain

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2:3on average), and build new train-dev-test splits with 1509, 150and350sentences for train, dev and test respectively. Training sets have around 10 hours of supervision. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets. We merge monolingual datasets into a single multilingual dataset, with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We collect between one and three recordings for each sentence (2:3on average)

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: Our 102 languages cover various language families and geographical locations (see Table 8), from Westem Europe/Americas, Eastem Europe, Central-Asia, Middle-East, North-Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, South-East Asia to CJK languages.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Intemet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Westem European group (with 11.5 average WER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (26.7 average WER) or South Asian (20.7), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and V oxPopuli.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Reducing the gaps across geographical groups is an important research direction for future work building on XTREME-S. We note that the tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. In general, speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The training sets of XTREME-S range from a few hours to a few hundred hours of labeled data per language. This is a few-shot setting suited for low-resource understanding. XTREME-S strongly encourages data-efficient self-supervised representation leaming. XTREME-S covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval.
